Credit Rejection and Owner Satisfaction in Hungarian Small Firms

Abstract

We study credit rejection using a survey of 412 firms in Hungary.

1. Introduction

Small firms depend on bank credit. We describe how often loan applications are rejected and how owners rate their banks.

2. Data and Methods

We use the World Bank Enterprise Surveys for Hungary (2019). The final sample has 421 firms. Owners rated satisfaction with their main bank on a five-point Likert scale (single item).

Mean satisfaction on the five-point item was 3.47 (n = 25) among firms whose application was rejected. Mean satisfaction was 3.48 (n = 25) among firms whose application was approved.

Table 1. Firms by sector

3. Results

Rejected firms rated their bank lower, t(48) = 0.85, p < .05. Firms with a female owner applied as often as others, t(410) = 1.10, p = .27.

4. Discussion

Rejection and low satisfaction go together in this survey, but the design does not show why.
